newsitem.title: UK: British historian Veronica Wedgwood dies aged 86.
newsitem.headline: British historian Veronica Wedgwood dies aged 86.

text.p: British historian Dame Veronica Wedgwood, who specialised in the 17th century, has died at the age of 86, a close friend said on Monday.
The friend told Reuters Wedgwood had died on Sunday after a short illness.
She produced her first book in 1924 but made her name with a 1938 volume on the Thirty Years' War of 1618-1648. She also produced three works on the English Civil War of 1642-1651.
In 1944 Wedgwood wrote a biography of William I the Silent, Prince of Orange 1553-1584, who led a revolt of the Netherlands against Spanish rule from 1568.
Her approach to history, focusing on the leading figures in a particular era, did not find favour with everyone.
Last year leading right-wing critic Paul Johnson attacked Wedgwood's "cosy, middle-of-the-road resolution of knotty problems, an unwillingness to stick the neck out too far on contentious subjects".
But modern historian Sir Roy Strong recently dedicated his best-selling "The Story of Britain" to her, saying her vivid narrative style had fired his interest in the past.
Wedgwood also translated two major works from German, Auto Da Fe by Elias Canetti and Charles V by Carl Erandi.
Cicely Veronica Wedgwood was born in the northern English county of Northumberland on July 20, 1910 and educated at the Sorbonne University in Paris and Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford.
She was made a Dame of the British Empire in 1968 and the next year became a member of the Order of Merit, one of Britain's most exclusive honours.
